diet.text: Almost only crayfish - mostly freshly moulted ones

overview.text: The Queen Snake is a harmless water snake of eastern North America that eats almost nothing but crayfish. It needs clean, rocky streams, so it disappears where streams become polluted.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: East of the Mississippi from western New York and south-western Ontario to Wisconsin and south to Alabama and northern Florida, with an isolated population in Arkansas.

habitat.text: Only clean running streams with stony or rocky bottoms, where the water stays at least about 10 °C while it is active.

diet.text: A real specialist: it hunts by day and eats crayfish, mostly ones that have just shed their hard shell. It finds them by smelling a chemical they give off while moulting.

reproduction.text: Mates in spring or autumn and gives birth to live young. After autumn mating, the female can wait until spring to give birth.

funfacts.text: It eats almost only soft, freshly moulted crayfish - it can smell when they are moulting.
